sense: a side view of a face

terms.gloss: a profile, a side view (of a portrait)
evidence: Plin. NH 35.56: catagrapha … hoc est oblīquās imāginēs
terms.comment: Pliny’s phrase for the portrait seen from the side, which Lewis & Short renders “a side-likeness, profile” (s.v. oblīquus). Oblīquus is slanting, sidelong: oblīquō capite, with the head turned (Plin. NH 8.88).
The Greek painters’ term, which Pliny explains with oblīquae imāginēs; a word for art history, not for everyday use.

terms.gloss: a sketch, an outline; a short profile of a person
evidence: Cic. Or. 103 (Lewis & Short): a sketch, outline
M-O s.v. silhouette: adumbrātiō vītae, a biographical sketch
terms.comment: For a written profile of someone, Morgan–Owens gives adumbrātiō (alicujus) vītae. Classically a sketch, and also a mere show or pretence (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: pīnxit et Antigonī rēgis imāginem alterō lūmine orbātī prīmus excōgitātā ratiōne vitia condendī; oblīquam namque fēcit, ut, quod deerat corporī, pictūrae deesse potius vidērētur
phrases.english: he also painted King Antigonus, who had lost an eye, and was the first to think of a way of hiding defects: he painted him in profile, so that what the body lacked might seem rather to be lacking in the picture

sources: Lewis & Short: obliquus · Lewis & Short: catagraphus · Lewis & Short: adumbratio · Lewis & Short: imago
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. forms: silhouette: profile.
